subtype: Approach: attending everything out of fear of falling behind [Pitfall]
passage: Kunal's Monday began at six with the physics batch and ended at nine-thirty with the maths batch, with school, a crowded bus and a cold paratha in between. At lunch Zubin, his desk-mate, rubbed his eyes. “Half of Saturday's chemistry is what school already taught,” Zubin said. “Skip it?” “And if that's the class where they give the trick?” Kunal said. “If everyone sits, I sit.” He copied every board note, filled two notebooks a week and never reread one. On the next test he scored exactly what he had scored three months earlier. Kunal stared at the paper, too tired to be surprised. That night he fell asleep with the notebook lying open on his face.

qa.q: Which class did Zubin say repeated what school had taught?
What might Kunal be worried about when he says everyone sits, so he sits?
qa.a: Falling behind the others, or missing the one class where the trick is given.

qa.q: What could Kunal try instead, and why?
qa.a: He could find out which classes really explain new ideas and use the freed time to practise problems, since sitting through lectures leaves no room to absorb anything.

qa.q: How does Kunal's routine look to Zubin?
qa.a: Zubin sees a tired desk-mate copying notes that are never reread, and thinks the batches he could skip are only costing him energy.

grounding: A student attends every batch out of fear of falling behind, and exhausting days leave marks unchanged.
